topic: When AI Multi-Agent Workflows Break Distributed State
postText:
We gave three autonomous agents tool access to orchestrate clinical resource allocations across disparate backend services. Agent A reserved telemetry monitors, Agent B assigned specialized lab panels, and Agent C crashed on a schema validation error while notifying duty teams.

The result? Hardware monitors stayed locked, lab orders sat unverified in database records, and the execution chain died silently mid-flight. The autonomous coordinator hallucinated partial completion, leaving persistent ghost reservations in our core infrastructure.

Multi-agent frameworks fail when engineers treat non-deterministic LLMs as distributed transaction coordinators. LLMs cannot guarantee atomicity. When multi-agent systems trigger irreversible side effects across APIs without deterministic control:
1. Context loss causes agents to forget partial mutations.
2. Incomplete execution leaves orphan records in downstream microservices.
3. Blind retries produce duplicate mutation payloads.

The architectural solution is separating dynamic planning from transactional execution using the Saga pattern. Autonomous agents propose an execution DAG, but a deterministic state machine executes the tool calls sequentially against a persistent journal. If any downstream agent fails, the state machine steps backward, executing idempotent compensating actions to clean up prior mutations.

Keep reasoning in the agent. Keep transactional integrity in deterministic code.
